card.name: Condition nouns before 'where' clauses
card.fires_on: The final noun naming a condition, patient group or procedure (pain, infections, patients, procedures, arthritis) in a dosing sentence. It comes right where a qualifier such as 'where', 'in which' or 'requiring' could follow.

modes.label: Condition noun
modes.description: A disease or symptom noun that ends a noun phrase, such as infections, pain, arthritis or disorders.
modes.example: For all other urinary tract<< infections>> the usual dosage is 2 g per

modes.label: Patient or procedure noun
modes.description: A patient group or procedure noun that ends a phrase and sets up a dosing condition.
modes.example: For pediatric<< patients>> with severe renal impairment or on dialysis

card.writes: It promotes the word 'where' in several languages, so it predicts a clause that restricts the setting.
card.plain: It fires on the noun that names the condition or patient group, just before a phrase like 'where' or 'in which' would add a restriction.
